provenance.note: Generated by drivers/survival on the pystatsval harness against a PyPI-installed pystatistics==4.2.1. 4.2.1 closes the last conf_int gap (DiscreteTimeSolution.conf_int) and adds DIRECT GPU validation of the one GPU-capable survival path, discrete_time, on the real survival::flchain cohort. Correctness for KM / log-rank / Cox / discrete-time fits both pystatistics and R survival on the identical survival::lung rows; discrete-time CPU correctness is extended to the large real flchain person-period design vs R glm(binomial). The GPU study expands flchain to person-period at calendar bin widths (yearly ~83k -> quarterly ~320k -> monthly ~952k rows) and a synthetic person-period scale-up grid, timing the binomial GLM fit (the operation the GPU accelerates) on CPU vs MPS (powerhouse) and CPU vs CUDA fp32 / fp64 (forge). Hosts: powerhouse (Apple Silicon, CPU fp64 + Metal/MPS fp32, R 4.5.2 / survival 3.8.3); forge (NVIDIA CUDA, CPU fp64 + CUDA fp32/fp64).
provenance.baseline: Compare against reports/survival-v4.2.0.md (the prior frozen report). Correctness vs R is bit-for-bit unchanged; 4.2.1 adds the discrete-time GPU device-pivot, the real-data flchain CPU-vs-R discrete-time correctness, and the float32 acceptance-boundary study (A6 / RIGOR R9).

r.engine: R survival::survfit / survdiff / coxph; glm(binomial) for discrete-time

reference.name: R survival::survfit / survdiff / coxph
reference.what: The R survival package (Therneau): survfit() for Kaplan-Meier, survdiff() for the log-rank test, coxph() for proportional hazards. Discrete-time survival is validated against R glm(family=binomial) on the identical person-period design pystatistics builds internally — on both the small survival::lung design and the large real survival::flchain design.

studies.title: Correctness vs R survival — Powerhouse (CPU / fp64), per quantity
Discrete-time CPU vs R on real flchain (~83k person-period rows), per quantity
Wall-clock vs R on survival::lung — Powerhouse (CPU / fp64)
studies.note: Per-fit median over timed repeats. With the 4.2.0 O(n log n) Cox PH, all four procedures are within a small constant factor of R on the tiny lung dataset; the scaling studies below carry the asymptotic and at-scale claims.

studies.title: Cox PH CPU scaling vs R — Powerhouse (CPU / fp64)
studies.note: Synthetic proportional-hazards DGP. pystatistics Cox PH is O(n log n) (vectorized reverse-cumsum risk sets + a Fenwick-tree concordance), matching R's complexity: the pystatistics/R wall ratio is FLAT at ~1-2.6x across n=250..8000.

studies.title: Discrete-time GPU fit scaling — Powerhouse: CPU (fp64) vs MPS (fp32)
studies.note: Wall-clock of the binomial GLM fit on the person-period design (expansion excluded — see the breakdown study). MPS acc cells are blank where the float32 fit fails loud: on the real discrete-time design the low-hazard baseline-interval dummies are unresolvable in float32 as the grid refines (see the float32 boundary study). MPS holds only on coarse grids; the robust large-scale GPU path is CUDA gpu_fp64 (Forge).

studies.title: Discrete-time float32 acceptance boundary — Powerhouse (MPS): accurate when accepted, fails loud when wrong
studies.note: Per bin granularity: the float32 acceptance gate accepts MPS exactly when the fit is float32-accurate (coef_max_rel ~1e-5 vs CPU) and rejects it as the grid refines. forced_max_rel is the RIGOR-R9 check — the accuracy of the REJECTED fit if forced: up to ~0.9, i.e. genuinely wrong, so the rejection is a correct fail-loud (A6), not a false negative. faithfulness_rel confirms the fit-isolated measurement reproduces the public discrete_time coefficients (~0).

studies.title: Expansion vs fit vs end-to-end — Powerhouse (CPU): the GLM fit dominates
studies.note: The person-period expansion is a pure-Python double loop, but it is a small fraction of end-to-end discrete_time at scale — the binomial GLM fit dominates, which is why the GPU speedup is reported on the fit.

studies.title: R glm(binomial) at scale on the flchain person-period design — Powerhouse
studies.note: R glm wall-clock climbs into the minutes at ~1M person-period rows (the model matrix is multi-GB); finer binning pushes the design past practical memory. This is the scale at which the exact CUDA gpu_fp64 path (Forge) is the practical option — the headline being that discrete-time survival runs on a GPU at all.

studies.title: Discrete-time GPU fit scaling — Forge: CPU (fp64) vs CUDA gpu_fp64 (exact)
studies.note: The robust large-scale path: CUDA backend='gpu_fp64' is numerically exact (see the precision study) and accepted at every granularity, including the monthly ~1M-row design — ~26x faster than the same-host CPU fp64 fit (105s -> 4.0s). Wall-clock of the binomial GLM fit on the person-period design (expansion excluded).

studies.title: Discrete-time GPU fit scaling — Forge: CPU (fp64) vs CUDA (fp32)
studies.note: CUDA float32 holds further than MPS: accepted (and fast) up through quarterly bins (~320k rows); the monthly cell is blank because the float32 fit fails loud there (the optimum is not stationary in float32). For exact fits at every scale use gpu_fp64 (above).

studies.title: Discrete-time GPU precision — Forge (CUDA): fp32 holds through quarterly, fp64 exact throughout
studies.note: CUDA fp32 (backend='gpu') is accepted and accurate to ~1e-5..1e-3 vs CPU across this sweep; CUDA gpu_fp64 is exact (~1e-13) at every granularity. Contrast the Powerhouse/MPS boundary study, where float32 fails loud from yearly bins onward — the float32 reach is platform-dependent, the exact gpu_fp64 path is not.

record_fields.max_abs: max absolute difference between pystatistics and R over a quantity's elements
record_fields.max_rel: max relative difference between pystatistics and R over a quantity's elements (correctness headline)
record_fields.n_elements: number of scalar elements compared for that quantity (1 for scalars, vector length otherwise)
record_fields.speedup_vs_r: R wall-clock / pystatistics wall-clock on the same fit (>1 means pystatistics is faster)
record_fields.ratio_pystat_over_r: pystatistics wall-clock / R wall-clock at a given n (flat across n once both are O(n log n))
record_fields.peak_mem_mb: peak memory during the fit (GPU allocator high-water mark; process RSS delta on CPU)
record_fields.coef_max_rel: max relative difference of the float32 GPU covariate coefficients vs the CPU fp64 fit (float32 tier ~1e-5 when accepted)
record_fields.forced_max_rel: RIGOR R9: max relative error of the REJECTED float32 fit if forced (large -> the fit is genuinely wrong -> the rejection is a correct fail-loud)
record_fields.faithfulness_rel: max relative difference between regression.fit on the reconstructed person-period design and the public discrete_time coefficients (~0 -> the fit-isolated measurement is faithful)
record_fields.expansion_frac_of_e2e: person-period expansion time / end-to-end discrete_time time (small at scale -> the GLM fit dominates)
